haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, with a pending row in the same transaction. Then Postgres is copied with a 1-second timeout. If Postgres fails, the caller still gets success and the pending row stays.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming row's version is higher than the stored version. The copy must also hold the advisory lock and find no tombstone for that user.
haiku-low.q3: Every running instance must report dual in app_flag_value, then one more minute must pass. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: It pauses while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5, rechecking every 10 seconds. It also reads the replica in batches of 2,000 rows.
haiku-low.q5: Reads need a clean comparer pass and a stepped flag ramp to 100%. The source of truth moves only after 3 days at 100%, a clean comparer pass within 24 hours, and an empty pending table.
haiku-low.q6: The pending row in MySQL users_pg_pending, written in the same transaction as the write. The sweeper, every 5 seconds, re-reads the user and copies or deletes it in Postgres.
haiku-low.q7: copy_to_pg runs under the per-user advisory lock and skips tombstoned users. delete_in_pg writes the tombstone under the same lock, so a late copy cannot re-insert the user.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres migration_progress.last_id, updated in the same transaction as each batch. It stops when a batch returns no rows, which is recorded in migration_progress.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer walks id ranges and compares every column, flagging one-sided rows and tombstoned ids. Differences surviving a one-minute recheck count as mismatches and get a pending row for repair.
haiku-low.q10: Instances go paused and are confirmed, then wait 5 seconds, so no instance can still be on dual. If steps 2 and 3 take over 20 seconds after that wait, set the flag back to dual.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres's identity sequence assigns ids after the switch, set with setval to the larger of MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT and max(id)+1 over users and tombstones. After rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set past the Postgres sequence value.
haiku-low.q12: Each Postgres write adds a users_mysql_pending row that the sweeper copies to MySQL, and deletes bump seq. Rollback pauses writes, drains the backlog, sets AUTO_INCREMENT, then sets dual. It ends at step 10, pg_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first (commit to MySQL together with a pending row, source of truth), then the Postgres copy is attempted (1 s timeout). If Postgres fails or times out, it is logged and counted, the pending row stays, and the caller still sees success.
sonnet.q2: Only if the stored version is lower than the incoming version (ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE users.version < EXCLUDED.version). Also nothing is done if a tombstone exists for the user.
sonnet.q3: Dual writes must be confirmed: every running instance reports users.write_mode=dual in app_flag_value (instance count equals running instances), plus one more minute of waiting. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change (flag cache refresh).
sonnet.q4: Before each batch it waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5, rechecking every 10 seconds. It reads from the replica (not the primary) in batches of 2,000 rows, and only one backfill runner is allowed at a time (advisory lock).
sonnet.q5: Reads: the backfill is done and the comparer has produced one clean full pass with zero mismatches (pending table nearly empty); then raise 1, 10, 50, 100% with at least 5 minutes each. Source of truth: 3 days soak at 100% reads, last comparer pass clean and started within the last 24 hours, and users_pg_pending empty.
sonnet.q6: A pending row in the MySQL table users_pg_pending (user_id, seq, created_at), written in the same MySQL transaction as the write. The sweeper (every 5 s, rows older than 5 s) re-reads the user from the MySQL primary and calls copy_to_pg (or delete_in_pg if the row is gone), then deletes the pending row with a seq check.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: delete_in_pg inserts a row into user_tombstones under the per-user advisory lock, and copy_to_pg, under the same lock, does nothing if a tombstone exists for the user. Tombstones are kept.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres table migration_progress (name, last_id). It is updated in the same Postgres transaction as the batch's copy_to_pg calls, so it is never ahead or behind. The backfill stops when a batch returns no rows, which is recorded in migration_progress.
sonnet.q9: The comparer job, which walks both tables in id ranges and compares all columns. It flags rows on only one side and Postgres rows with a tombstone. It skips ids with pending rows and re-checks other differences against MySQL primary and Postgres after one minute. A surviving difference counts as a mismatch, and the comparer creates a pending row for that user so the normal repair path fixes it.
sonnet.q10: Writes are first set to paused (retryable 503), confirmed on all instances plus 5 more seconds, so no instance can still be on dual. Then pending is drained, the sequence is set, and write_mode is set to pg_primary. If steps 2 and 3 are not finished 20 s after the 5 s wait, set write_mode=dual; writes resume on MySQL within 30 s (about 85 s total) and nothing has changed.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids through the identity sequence (GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY). Before the switch it is set with setval to the larger of MySQL's next AUTO_INCREMENT (read with information_schema_stats_expiry=0) and max(id)+1 over Postgres users and user_tombstones. On rollback, run ALTER TABLE users AUTO_INCREMENT = <Postgres sequence value> so MySQL can't reuse an id Postgres issued.
sonnet.q12: In pg_primary mode each write commits to Postgres with a row in users_mysql_pending, and the sweeper copies to MySQL (version rule); the comparer runs daily in both directions. Rollback: set paused and confirm plus 5 s, wait for users_mysql_pending to be empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to the Postgres sequence value, set write_mode=dual (and read_from_pg to 0 if needed), with the same 90 s budget and abort rule (set pg_primary again if over 20 s). The option ends at step 10, when pg_only is confirmed on all instances (at least 14 days after step 8, clean comparer, empty pending).
